articles.title: FDA Caught Suppressing Vaccine Risk Evidence for Children — Deaths Already Recorded, Warnings Ignored

No action has been taken, and the suppression appears deliberate — protecting the vaccine program over the children it was supposed to protect. This is regulatory capture in its most lethal form.

articles.title: Theranos Whistleblower Tyler Shultz Slams Holmes Documentary for Whitewashing a Fraud That Endangered Patients

The real story — how regulators, investors, and media enablers failed — remains untold.

articles.title: Curcumin Demonstrates Potent Anticancer Activity in Sarcoma Cells — Even Memorial Sloan Kettering Admits It Works
articles.summary: A new study confirms curcumin's balanced anticancer profile in sarcoma cell lines, adding to over 5,000 years of traditional use and a growing body of peer-reviewed evidence. Even the establishment's own Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center acknowledges turmeric's therapeutic history — yet oncology protocols remain locked on patented chemotherapy regimens with far greater toxicity. The question is no longer whether curcumin works; it's why it remains outside standard-of-care guidelines.

articles.title: Estrogen Dominance, Endotoxin, and the Hormonal Chaos Medicine Won't Explain to You
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov breaks down the interconnected roles of estrogen, histamine, serotonin, and endotoxin in driving chronic disease — a framework that contradicts the pharmaceutical model of isolated symptoms requiring isolated drugs. Blood estrogen levels routinely mislead clinicians while tissue-level dominance wreaks havoc on energy, fertility, and neurological function. This is the metabolic science that doesn't generate drug sales, which is precisely why you've never heard your doctor explain it.

articles.title: Decanoic Acid Found to Suppress Dangerous Inflammation — Could Replace High-Dose Steroids Pharma Profits From
articles.summary: Peer-reviewed research published in PLOS ONE shows decanoic acid — a naturally occurring medium-chain fatty acid — additively suppresses IL-1β inflammatory signaling and enables significant dose-sparing of dexamethasone in macrophage models. This means a cheap, non-patentable compound could reduce dependence on synthetic glucocorticoids whose adverse side effects are well-documented and profitable to manage. Don't expect this to show up in clinical guidelines anytime soon.

The science has been quietly more complicated than the approved narrative admits.
